Volume One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperial Court Attendant, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
1. The Section on the Ritual for Supreme Accomplishment. First: Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the palace of Vaiśravaṇa.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
with the Great Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, as their leader;
as well as countless devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
As well as Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors (Lokapālas), Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara,
Ratnapāṇi, Pūrṇabhadra, Bala, Mahābala, Nandikeśvara, Mahākāla, and Dhanvantari.
Together with the various celestial queens and others,
each accompanied by countless hundreds of thousands of retinues,
there were also great hosts of rākṣasas.
They are the rākṣasa lord Suvarṇa, the ten-headed rākṣasa lord,
the rākṣasa lord Vaiśravaṇa, the rākṣasa lord Ratnaguhya,
the rākṣasa lord Cāruguhya, and the rākṣasa lord Anantaguhyaka.
The Rākṣasa Lord Samantagupta, the Rākṣasa Lord Datta,
the Rākṣasa Lord Durdaṃṣṭra, the Rākṣasa Lord Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭra,
the Rākṣasa Lord Ucchuṣma, and the Rākṣasa Lord Gajamukha.
In this manner, the rākṣasa lords each led hundreds of thousands of koṭis of retinues and gathered for the assembly.
Furthermore, there was a great host of yakṣas,
namely the yakṣa lord Puruṣa-ṛṣi and the yakṣa lord Aṭavaka.
The Yakṣa Lord Well-Tamed, the Yakṣa Lord Radiant Light,
the Yakṣa Lord Fine Appearance, the Yakṣa Lord Wondrous Light,
the Yakṣa Lord Wondrous Eyes, and the Yakṣa Lord Viśeṣan.
The yakṣa lord Subhakeśa, the yakṣa lord Durākāra,
the yakṣa lord Vijayin, the yakṣa lord Jvalanta,
the yakṣa lord Agniśikha, and the yakṣa lord Yaśasvin.
The yakṣa lord Khañjika, the yakṣa lord Puṣpadatta,
the yakṣa lord Puṣpaketu, the yakṣa lord Ratnaśikha,
the yakṣa lord Vipuladhana, and the yakṣa lord Suprabuddha.
The yakṣa lord Kalyāṇakārin, the yakṣa lord Subāhu,
the yakṣa lord Suvibhūṣita, the yakṣa lord Maṇidaṃṣṭra,
the yakṣa lord Surīya, and the yakṣa lord Sūryaprabha.
The yakṣa lord Divānanda, the yakṣa lord Vivṛtadanta,
the yakṣa lord Jvalanaprabha, the yakṣa lord Bhīṣmavaktra, the yakṣa lord Samantaprabha, and other such yakṣa lords.
Possessing great majestic power and moving freely through the air,
each led countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of retinues as they gathered for this assembly.
Furthermore, the hosts of great Vidyādharas,
up to and including the hosts of great Ṛṣis, all gathered together.
The Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, surrounded by a retinue of hundreds of thousands of koṭis, attended upon the World-Honored One.
At that time, there was a deity named Naṇḍa,
whose physical appearance was exceptionally sublime and who bore a smile upon his face;
he held the sun, the moon, and various ritual implements in his hands.
Adorned with various jewels, its radiance surpasses that of the sun and moon;
it has the two nāgas Nanda and Upananda as armlets and the Takṣaka nāga as a waist-belt.
Possessing great power like that of Nārāyaṇa,
he too came to the assembly and sat before the Buddha.
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa rose from his seat.
With various precious flowers, as well as *paṭma* flowers,
*kumuda* flowers, *puṇḍarīka* flowers,
*utpala* flowers, and *saugandhika* flowers.
With *vārṣika* flowers, *campaka* flowers,
*māndārava* flowers, and *mahāmāndārava* flowers—
with such various flowers of both water and land, they made offerings to the Buddha.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] a thousand times and prostrated at his feet,
he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
I see this assembly of great yakṣas and great rākṣasas."
While manifesting various forms that devour human beings,
he further saw a great assembly of Bodhisattvas, a great assembly of Vidyādharīs, and a great assembly of Ṛṣis,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and other such hosts, all of whom had gathered and were surrounding the World-Honored One.
I have never before seen such a great auspicious omen.
What Dharma does the World-Honored One intend to teach now?
Is it the teaching on the secret maṇḍala?
"Please teach us the Dharma of samādhi.
World-Honored One, now is precisely the right time; we pray that you will expound it extensively.
At that time, the World-Honored One accepted the request of King Vaiśravaṇa.
And he immediately said:
"O Heavenly King, I see that all sentient beings in the world experience great terror throughout the day and night."
It is because there are immeasurable and most wicked yakṣas and rākṣasas who,
watching for an opportunity, seek to cause harm.
O Heavenly King, those most wicked yakṣas and rākṣasas—
"Now you have taken refuge in me within my teaching;
receive the three refuges and the precepts,
and henceforth do not harm any sentient beings."
At that time, having thus comforted the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa,
the World-Honored One immediately entered the samādhi called "Subduing the Fiery Radiance of Yakṣas."
Within that meditative concentration, his body emitted a great radiance,
which universally illuminated the trichiliocosm.
All the great and wicked yakṣas therein—
The rākṣasas, piśācas, bhūtas,
as well as the malevolent nāgas and even the lunar mansions and planets—
once illuminated by the Buddha’s light, they were all awakened.
That light circled back, revolving three times around the Buddha, and entered the crown of his head.
It then emerged from the Buddha’s face and entered the crown of the head of the Nanda-deva.
At that time, once the light had entered the crown of the Nanda-deva’s head—
He immediately manifested a great body like Mount Sumeru;
his face bore an expression of wrath, yet he also displayed a laughing countenance,
and he possessed a thousand arms.
Holding a kapāla and various weapons,
with a tiger-skin draped across his chest and the kapāla serving as his ornament,
he blazes with radiant light and possesses great majestic power.
When the Nanda deity manifested this body,
the great earth shook and all who beheld it were struck with fear;
at that time, the Nanda deity joined his palms toward the Buddha.
He addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I possess a heart-mantra that is well able to subdue the hosts of asuras,
as well as all yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, and so forth."
It even causes Mahābrahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Maheśvara to all submit and be subdued;
it is also able to summon the multitudes of all devas and nāgas.
"Bhagavān, this heart-mantra of mine is the supreme method for accomplishment for all vidyādharas;
therefore, I now [declare it] within this assembly."
I wish to expound this extensively before the Tathāgata,
so that all vidyādharas may attain accomplishment and swiftly fulfill the aspirations within the hearts of all sentient beings.
Furthermore, Blessed One, this heart-mantra (hṛdaya) shall bring accomplishment in all places through recitation;
it even enables one to enter all maṇḍalas and various samādhis.
In all the maṇḍalas belonging to these families— the Tathāgata family,
the Vajra family, the Ratna family, the Padma family, and the Karma family—
one shall attain accomplishment by reciting this heart-mantra of mine.
Furthermore, one shall gain entry into all samādhis, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and dharmas,
even attaining the great dhāraṇī.
O Bhagavān, regarding these mantras, seals, and signs of the maṇḍala-dharma of the equality of all families:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, out of compassion, will graciously accept me and permit me to proclaim [this teaching].
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the god Nanda, saying:
"Regarding all the various classes of the Samaya Maṇḍala of Equal Dharma, there are the vidyā-mantras, mudrās, and signs."
I also rejoice. You, Nanda, O Deva, should now swiftly proclaim this for the sake of all vidyādharas.
Then, Nanda Deva, having received the holy command of the Buddha, [did so].
For the sake of benefiting [all beings], he circumambulated the Buddha three times, stood before the Buddha,
and then spoke this heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mahāvidyā*): *athato vāridatodhavobhiḍabhaṭa*.

Recite this vidyā-mantra once more.

Recite the heart-mantra once to empower it.
Within the maṇḍala, burn agallochum incense and recite the heart-mantra once;

Again, reciting the heart-mantra, he empowered white mustard seeds and struck the flask;

Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a *ṣaḍaṅga* (demon) to move and act,
first prepare an unguent using white sandalwood, *kunkuma*, and other such fragrances,

Thereafter, burn agalloch incense,
snap the fingers, and recite the heart-mantra to empower it;
the *sattva* will then move of its own accord and return to its original place.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause an animal to speak of matters,
one should burn agalloch incense over the ashes and white mustard seeds.
Having recited the heart-mantra twenty-one times while empowering them, [one should proceed].
Thereafter, recite the heart-mantra again.
By throwing ashes and mustard seeds onto the body of a beast, it will immediately speak of matters.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a young girl to speak of matters:

select a young girl who is of handsome appearance and possesses complete physical features.
Having bathed and purified oneself, one should don new white garments,
sit within the maṇḍala,
make offerings of various flowers, and burn agallochum incense.
He will then be able to recount events of the past, present, and future.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a youth to speak of matters,
one should use white mustard seeds mixed with the ashes of *jiti*.
Recite the heart-mantra once to empower it,
burn agalloch incense to fumigate it, and then cast it upon the crown of the youth’s head;
he will immediately recount the matter.
Furthermore, if one wishes to subdue fire so that it does not burn,
one should take firewood and recite the Heart Mantra over it once while performing the empowerment.
Having burned *安息香* (anxi-xiang) incense and fumigated [the object], one places it within the fire;

Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to suppress various heterodox spells.
One should use a clean white thread,
empower it once by reciting the heart-mantra,
and fumigate it with agallochum incense.
Tie it to the left arm of the practitioner;
all malevolent spells will be completely subdued.

One should use cow dung that has not fallen to the ground to smear the maṇḍala.
Place a mūrdhagata within the maṇḍala,
make offerings with various flowers, and burn agallochum incense as an offering.
Recite the heart-mantra once to empower it.
This Manograha is capable of accomplishing feats of siddhi and can furthermore cause things to move at will.
If one enters a battle array while reciting this *mantra*, one will naturally achieve victory;
even forests, mountains, and rocks can be destroyed.
Whatever deeds a practitioner undertakes shall all be accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment for a bow,
one should take guggulu incense, recite the heart mantra over it once with empowerment,
and burn it as an offering of incense.
One will then be able to accomplish whatever rites one desires at will.
Furthermore, if one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment using a trident,
construct a maṇḍala as before.
Then, recite the heart-mantra once.
Having empowered the agallochum incense and burned it to fumigate the trident,
place it within the maṇḍala and again recite the heart-mantra once.
At that time, the trident immediately emitted a blazing light;
it rose up, leaving the ground, and moved toward the four directions,
before returning and entering back into the maṇḍala.
The rite of accomplishment is performed according to the practitioner's intention.
Furthermore, if one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment for a sword,
one likewise uses guggulu incense and recites the heart-mantra.
Recite the empowerment mantra once and burn it as incense;
this will also enable the accomplishment of all tasks.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to cause a khaṭvāṅga to perform the rite of accomplishment, [one should proceed as follows].
One should take the ashes of *citikā* and, having empowered them once by reciting the heart-mantra, smear them upon the *khaṭvāṅga*;
thus one will be able to accomplish all feats of siddhi.
Furthermore, if one wishes to perform the rite of accomplishment using a *kapāla*,
one should first paint the maṇḍala according to the ritual rules,
and then select a clean *kapāla* in accordance with the prescribed method.
Anoint it with white sandalwood incense and place it within the maṇḍala.
Burn agallochum incense and empower it by reciting the heart mantra once.
Then, whatever one undertakes will be accomplished and one will be able to move about;
furthermore, one will be able to speak of matters pertaining to the three periods of time.
Moreover, for this rite, one should employ a sharp sword while reciting the heart-mantra.
Having consecrated it once with the incense of guggulu,
the practitioner then recites the syllable HŪṂ aloud to empower that sword;
the sword immediately emits light and soars upward into the sky.
It shall return to its original place.
Furthermore, if one enters a battle formation, the enemy will retreat and be defeated.
Moreover, there is another method: if one wishes to cause the images in a celestial shrine to move, [one should perform the following].
Before that image, burn agalloch incense and recite the heart-mantra once;
at that time, the celestial image will move as one wishes.
Furthermore, according to another method,
if at any location on earth a practitioner suspects there is a hidden treasure and wishes to retrieve it,
they should immediately construct a maṇḍala upon that ground.
If one burns agalloch incense and recites the heart-mantra once,
hidden treasures will appear.
Furthermore, as another method, one may use white mustard seeds and empower them by reciting the heart-mantra once.
With these mustard seeds, one should cast them wherever appropriate—
whether in a village, in an empty house,
before an image in a deva-shrine, or at the site of a stupa or temple.
Even in places such as mountain crags and dragon pools,
wherever one casts [the substance], if one burns agalloch incense and recites the heart-mantra once,
whatever hidden treasures (nidhi) are there will all manifest.
Furthermore, there is another method: using white mustard seeds, recite the heart-mantra over them once to empower them.
Then, cast these seeds upon the body of the elephant and burn agalloch incense to fumigate it.
Furthermore, by reciting the heart-mantra once,
that elephant will follow the practitioner’s intent and skillfully perform tasks;
it may even cause a śatru to be destroyed according to one's wish.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate malaria for others or to provide protection,
one should take ashes and white mustard seeds mixed with water,
recite the Heart Mantra once over them, and empower them.
Having burned *安息香* (anxi xiang) incense and fumigated [the object], one should wear it upon the body;
the malarial fever will then be cured, and one will obtain protection.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to cease all fears, [one should do as follows].
One should burn agalloch incense over a white thread while reciting the heart mantra once to empower it.
When worn around the neck, all fears will be immediately dispelled.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate various ailments,
one should take guggulu incense and empower it by reciting the heart-mantra once.
By burning and fumigating the body of the afflicted person, all illnesses will be immediately removed.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause the śrāddhas to attain *jvara*,
one should employ guggulu incense and empower it by reciting the heart-mantra once;
thus, thousands of śrāddhas will all attain *jvara*.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a śatru-jaṭhara-jvara to arise,
one should employ *humāsa* mixed with *guggulu*.
Recite the heart-mantra once for empowerment,
and by calling the name of Śatru seven times while performing homa, one will immediately attain the *ḍākinī* Jvālā.
If one wishes to cause her to cease [her activity], [perform the following].
Furthermore, by using agallochum incense and reciting the heart-mantra once to empower it, performing seven rounds of homa will immediately bring about cessation.
Another method: if one wishes to cause a śatru (enemy) [to be subdued]...
For one who has attained the *kīlana* (stake-driving) rite,
one should employ *guggulu* incense; then,
taking the name of the *śatru* (enemy), recite it together with the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya-mantra*).
Having performed the empowerment seven times,
cast it into the fire;
one will immediately attain the *ghṛhīta* (seizure) of *kīlana*.
If one wishes to cause it to cease,
one should empower ashes with the mantra once and place them upon the crown of the head; thus, it will be immediately pacified.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate various types of malarial fevers,
one should take a black thread, empower it by reciting the Heart Mantra once,
and tie it upon the arm; the illness will then be cured.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate various diseases,
one should mix seven kinds of grains with white mustard seeds, dip them in clarified butter,
and perform *homa* while reciting the heart-mantra; then [the illness] will be cured.
Furthermore, if one wishes to release those afflicted by various poisonous drugs,
one should take a peacock’s tail and recite the heart-mantra over it.
Having empowered it, one should brush it upon the person's body, and the poison will be immediately dispelled.
All the aforementioned dharmas are to be performed using guggulu incense;
by reciting the heart-mantra and consecrating them, all shall be accomplished.

Furthermore, drive these stakes into that *vārā*.

Or if [the victim] is nailed into a *śmaśāna* (charnel ground),

If [the victim] is pinned within the *śunarnīyagrodha* tree,

Alternatively, if one nails [the image] in front of Gītamāra,

by striking the maṇḍala with a mudgara,

Furthermore, if one wishes to command yakṣas and rākṣasas,
one should fashion or paint their images and then recite the great vidyā-mantra.
Having empowered the mṛnāla once,

it reveals all hidden treasures and even provides an abundance of wealth and grain.

one should fashion or paint his image.

One should fulfill all the wishes of those who practice this rite, providing them with all necessities such as wealth and grain.

One should go to a place where there is an image of Vaiśravaṇa,

answering all questions as desired and even leading them to the location where hidden treasures lie buried.
Furthermore, mix white mustard seeds with ashes;
recite the Great Mantra over them seven times for empowerment,
place them upon the crown of the Vaiśravaṇa image, and burn agalloch incense.

Then that Vaiśravaṇa, together with his hundred attendants,

Furthermore, burn agalloch incense before the image.

With the three karmas purified, one’s lifespan will increase by a thousand years;
furthermore, all ritual procedures for accomplishment will be successfully achieved.

If the practitioner applies this medicine to his forehead,

If one dots [the forehead] at the heart, one attains invisibility;
one may go or stay as one pleases without any obstruction.
If one dots [the forehead] at the eyes, all hidden treasures will become visible.

If one takes this medicine, one’s lifespan will be extended for hundreds of thousands of kalpas,

If one applies it to the body, the body immediately becomes as firm and solid as a vajra.
Furthermore, if a practitioner of the Dharma wishes to accomplish the sacred medicine:
One should mix the fat of a black ram with the ghee of a yellow cow.

If one recites the great mantra over it twenty-one times to empower it, it becomes a sacred medicine.
If this medicine is used to anoint the eyes,

Burning agalloch incense, recite the Great Mantra twenty-one times.

Drive in the kīla with the syllables *dru hṛiḥ na ya*.

All *ḍākinīs* who seek an opportunity shall be swiftly driven away.

Construct a ritual stake according to the rite;

Chapter Four: The Procedure for the Accomplishment of the Supreme Maṇḍala Rite. At that time, the deity Nanda again proclaimed the supreme rite of the great maṇḍala.
This maṇḍala can accomplish all celestial beings;
even Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and Maheśvara constantly come to take refuge in it,
and even all the ṛṣis constantly praise it.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will embrace and protect them;
all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others will attain samādhi;
and all vidyā-mantras and ritual procedures will be fully accomplished.
If there is a practitioner who wishes to construct this maṇḍala,
they should first select an auspicious site for accomplishment according to the ritual rules. Thereafter,
during the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day under a favorable planetary alignment, [they should proceed].
However, one may begin:
first, the practitioner bathes himself to become pure and puts on new white garments;
having eaten white food and drink, he proceeds.
Thereafter, one should construct a three-tiered maṇḍala using *gomaya* from a non-falling cow.
The outermost first tier shall measure thirty-two cubits in length and breadth,
complete with its proportions, four sides, and four gates.
That maṇḍala is perfectly complete and circular;
its second inner layer is made of white sandalwood,
measuring eight cubits in length and breadth.
The third inner layer is made of camphor and *kunkuma* (saffron) and measures four cubits in length and breadth.

Mahābrahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and so forth;

Next, place various flowers, fruits, and the production of food and drink;
there shall be eight hundred offerings of each type of flower and fruit,
and eight hundred lamps shall be lit.
Offer eight hundred portions of food for the birth [deities].
Offer thirty-two portions of food for the individual births.
Furthermore, offer one hundred and eight portions of food consisting of sixty-four flavors.
Furthermore, various insignia were placed;
additionally, eight hundred bowls were arranged interspersed with the insignia.
Next, thirty-two swords and one hundred and eight banners were set out.
Next, place eight mudgaras, eight tridents, four wheels, four conchs, four śaktis, thirty-two vajras, four pestles, four bells, and four dumaras.
And having offered various types of incense, flowers,
and so forth, one should then station a person at each of the four gates and four corners, clad in armor and holding weapons in hand.
On the four outer sides, use five colors to arrange various decorations and ornaments;
furthermore, set out a variety of musical performances.
At each time of offering food, one performs the musical offerings.
Having thus arranged the ritual procedures according to the dharma,
the practitioner then acts in accordance with the dharma.
Three times each day, one should offer food as an offering.
These offerings must all be consecrated seven times before being presented to the noble deities.
Subsequently, the practitioner should blend *guggulu* incense with white mustard seeds and sesame oil.
Having performed the homa according to the ritual rules before the maṇḍala,

Having paid homage to the World-Honored One, he addressed the practitioner, saying:
"Welcome! I shall now grant you whatever you seek.

That Naṭa deity said, "In accordance with the practitioner's intent;

[They seek] the status of a Vidyādhara, or Śakra Devendra, or a World-Protector (Lokapāla) and a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin),

Alternatively, one may subdue heterodox teachings, master the voices of animals,

The Section on the Mudrās and Great Mantras for Supreme Accomplishment, Part Seven. At that time, the deity Nanda further explained the method of mudrās.
This mudrā-form is the method for supreme accomplishment.
When a practitioner is about to perform the rite and bind the mudrā,
they must first cleanse both hands.
Furthermore, one should first apply fragrant ointment before forming the mudrā.
For the fundamental mudrā of Nanda, join the palms of both hands;
raise both middle fingers, and do the same for the little fingers.
The thumbs are like hooks;
the middle fingers are bent back like rings, and the index fingers are likewise.
This great mudrā possesses great majestic power.
It skillfully accomplishes all tasks,
even causing various beings to move and speak,
and it subdues yakṣas, rākṣasas, and others.
It may also be used for summoning.
Such matters as these will all be accomplished,
and one will also be able to accomplish all dharmas.
When forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:
Oṃ dhuru dhuru kuṃbha svāhā. Then, with the previous mudrā, bend the tips of the thumbs.
Place the middle fingers like vajras upon the crown of the head.
While forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:
Oṃ jñiti jñiti jñajñiti mūdrāra hūṃ. This mudrā and this mantra can accomplish all activities.
The heart-seal of Naṭarāja does not change from the previous seal;
with both hands joined like a vajra,

When forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:
Oṃ dhuru dhuru svāhā. This mudrā and this mantra are able to subdue all yakṣas and rākṣasas.
And for all the nāgas up to the various malevolent beings,
the heart-seals of the devas do not change from the previous seals;
one forms the seal by bending the two index fingers and extending the two thumbs upward.
When forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:
Oṃ naṭariṇi nivajraya hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mudrā and the great mantra.
It can accomplish all rites of siddhi.
For the heart-seal (*hṛdaya-mudrā*) of all yakṣas and rākṣasas:
with both hands palms flat, the index fingers, middle fingers, and thumbs are pressed tightly together to form the seal.
When forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:
Oṃ namo buddhāya vuddhiśvarāya naṭakuṃbharākṣasamukha mahāghonadhipate vaiśravaṇa suta hūṃ jñīḥ svāhā. This is the mudrā and the great mantra.
It thoroughly subdues all the planetary deities, as well as all the yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, and so forth.
When one binds this mudrā and recites the vidyā-mantra,
those yakṣas and others will all be utterly dispersed.
If you do not do so, your head shall split into seven pieces.
The seal of the gods does not differ from the previous seal;
one opens the two index fingers and extends the two little fingers.
When forming this mudrā, recite the great mantra:

One can also perform all rites of accomplishment (*sādhana*).

This great mantra possesses immense power.
If one burns agallochum incense empowered by this great vidyā-mantra,
all rites concerning the lunar mansions and planets will be accomplished.
Furthermore, the practitioner must first purify themselves.
Thereafter, recite this great vidyā-mantra twenty-one times to consecrate the guggulu incense;
then burn this incense before the daytime image of the deity Naṭarāja and offer white food.
However, if the practitioner recites this great vidyā one thousand times and completes the count,
the painted image will immediately move and emit light,
responding to the practitioner by saying:
"You have attained mastery in all the ritual manuals, maṇḍalas, and methods of accomplishment for the deity Nanda.
Once the practitioner has seen this auspicious omen, they should immediately present an offering of arghya."
From this point forward, all accomplishments (*siddhi*) performed by the practitioner shall be achieved.
Furthermore, one should employ *guggulu* incense while reciting the Great Mantra;
having empowered it, burn it to fumigate the sword.
Then, reciting the great mantra, one consecrates the sword;
immediately upon raising and moving it, it emits light and performs various deeds.
This extends to other weapons such as the trident, the wheel, the vajra, the pestle, the mātṛgaṇas, and the ḍākinīs.
One should empower and burn guggulu incense according to the previously described method;
immediately, [the image] will move, emit light, and be able to perform various deeds.
Furthermore, having empowered white mustard seeds by reciting the Great Mantra, one should strike the celestial image with them.
Again, reciting the Great Mantra and burning agalloch incense while fumigating the image, it immediately emits light,
reaching as far as Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, Vaiśravaṇa, Mahākāla, and the other gods.
Furthermore, as in the previous ritual, one should burn agallochum incense and recite the great mantra to empower the image, whereupon it will emit light.
Moreover, the practitioner should construct a maṇḍala according to the prescribed method.
Make offerings with incense, flowers, and so forth. Furthermore,
according to the ritual procedure, take an argha-vase, fill it completely with scented water,
and place it within the maṇḍala.
While burning agalloch incense and reciting the Great Mantra with empowerment,
the *argha* vase will spontaneously move and even emit light.
Furthermore, construct the maṇḍala as before.
Having made offerings with various kinds of incense and flowers,
one should apply fragrant ointment to the back of a clear mirror and place it within the maṇḍala.
Furthermore, take white mustard seeds and grain blossoms;
having empowered them by reciting the Great Mantra, strike the surface of the mirror.
Burn agalloch incense and recite the Great Mantra three times.
As soon as the mirror was moved, it emitted a great radiance;
through this mirror, one could perceive events of the past, present, and future,
and could also see the celestial realm of the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
One will be able to see everything down to the palaces of the nāgas and so forth;
furthermore, one will also be able to know the lifespans of oneself and others.
Moreover, the practitioner must first observe the precepts and maintain purity.
Having put on new, fine garments,
one should then take a *kapāla* that is endowed with the marks and signs according to the ritual rules,
and bathe it with scented water until it is perfectly pure.
One should apply fragrant ointments to it;
having first applied scented oil to the center,
the practitioner then uses five-colored powders.
Construct a square maṇḍala according to the ritual rules.
At the four gates of the maṇḍala,
place four argha vases filled with scented water.
Place four silver bowls filled with food offerings;
place flowers in four bowls;
and place four swords and five-colored banners.
Arranging them in such alternating patterns,
one should further place three *kapālas* at the center of the maṇḍala.
Then, take one of the previous *kapālas*,
recite the Great Mantra over it seven times for consecration,
and place it upon the three *kapālas*.
Furthermore, burn agalloch incense and recite the great mantra;
having empowered it, snap your fingers three times.
Thereupon, that kapāla will immediately emit light.
The practitioner gazes upon it and sees things just as they were in the mirror before;
eventually, he even comes to see the deity Nanda and his retinue,
who speak to the practitioner.
It is said that whatever the practitioner seeks shall be obtained according to their wishes.
Regarding the aforementioned maṇḍala and the methods for accomplishment, such as the kapāla and so forth,
this applies to all men and women alike.
One should generate a courageous, firm, and beneficial mind for the sake of others' welfare.
Those who perform this rite shall all achieve success,
with the sole exception of those who have committed the five great heinous crimes, those who slander the Buddha-dharma, and those who fail to recognize kindness and virtue.
Not only will they fail to achieve accomplishment, they shall also be unable to see or hear this Dharma.
Furthermore, if a practitioner wishes to enter the palaces of the asuras or the palaces of the nāgas:
One should recite the Great Mantra twenty-one times according to the ritual;
by burning agalloch incense, all shall be able to enter.
Furthermore, one should burn agalloch incense while reciting the Great Mantra.
Furthermore, one should strike the dragon pool with white mustard seeds and use stakes made of khadira wood to nail them into the dragon pool,
thereby effecting its subjugation.
If one wishes for it to be as it was before,
one should extract that stake and burn agalloch incense, and it will immediately return to its former state.
If one wishes to subdue an enemy army, [one should do so].
One should fashion a ritual stake from iron, recite the great mantra according to the rite twenty-one times to empower it,
and fumigate it with agallochum incense.
If one drives [a stake] into the base of a large tree, the enemy army will be immediately suppressed.
If one takes up that stake, it will return to its former state.
If one wishes to release those seized by the various planetary deities (graha), [one should perform this rite].
When burning guggulu incense and fumigating the body of the person being held,
one should recite the great mantra to empower white mustard seeds and water;
by sprinkling these upon that person's body, they will immediately be liberated and released.
If one wishes to eliminate various types of malarial fevers,
one should take a five-colored thread, recite the Great Mantra over it to empower it,
burn agalloch incense while fumigating it, and tie it upon the body of the patient; the malarial fever will then be cured.
If one wishes to be liberated from fetters and bonds,
one should recite the Great Mantra eight hundred times;
then all fetters and bonds will be completely liberated.
If one wishes to be liberated from shackles and fetters,
one should recite the Great Mantra with empowerment,
burn agalloch incense, and fumigate white mustard seeds.
If one strikes it, they will immediately fall off.
If one wishes to transfer thunder and hail to another location,
one should use branches of the pomegranate tree.
If one wishes to stop the rain, one should use branches of the *kharvīra* tree.
If one wishes to seek grain,
one should perform homa using the seven kinds of grain.
One will immediately obtain whatever one desires. If one wishes to cause rain to fall,
one should perform homa using sesame seeds and non-glutinous rice together.
Rain will fall immediately.
If one wishes to expel various yakṣas,
one should perform homa using chaff.
If one wishes to eliminate various diseases,
one should perform homa using sesame oil.
If one wishes to transfer poison to another location, [one should likewise perform homa].
One should use a peacock feather.
For those who seek peace and happiness,
if they simply maintain the recitation with sincere intent, they will always enjoy peace and happiness.
This great vidyā is effective for performing hundreds of thousands of methods of accomplishment;
one should recite it according to the ritual rules and employ guggulu incense.
All that is undertaken shall be accomplished; this dharma is the most preeminent among all dharmas.
This concludes the lower fascicle of the *Buddha-bhāṣita-parama-rahasya-naṭarāja-tantra*.
